newsitem.title: USA: US Apr spot natgas prices hold, March prices rise.
newsitem.headline: US Apr spot natgas prices hold, March prices rise.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for April 1 were little changed Wednesday, as nomination deadlines expired and traders stepped out to buy additional swing supplies before the end of the month, market sources said.
April Louisiana Gulf prices were unchanged in the low-$1.80s per mmBtu on most of the pipes, with Henry Hub quoted again at $1.82-1.87.
In south Texas, April prices failed to budge from Tuesday's values of about $1.75, with Houston Ship Channel quoted at $1.82-1.85.
For Thursday delivery, Gulf prices gained about three cents to $1.88-1.92, while south Texas prices were fairly steady in the low-to-mid $1.80s.

At the New York city-gate, swing prices were little changed at $2.16-2.21 as the stronger prices in the Gulf counteracted the weak demand in the Northeast. April pricing was up two to three cents at $2.17-2.19.
In the Appalachian region, April prices were slightly lower at $2.01-2.08.
Cooler temperatures are forecast for the Northeast this weekend and into early next week, Weather Services Corp said.
In West Texas, April 1 Permian prices were little changed in the mid-$1.60s. Swing gas prices climbed into the mid-to-high $1.70s as above-normal temperatures continued in the Southwest.
At the southern California border, April deals were reported done in the mid-$1.70s, while swing trading ranged from $1.85 to $1.91.
In the Midcontinent, April prices remained in the low-to-mid $1.70s, up about 10 cents from March indices. Swing prices were also steady in the mid-to-high $1.70s.
Chicago city-gate for next month was quoted about two cents lower at $1.94-1.95, while Detroit city-gate was talked at $2.05-2.10.

Temperatures throughout the Midwest are forecast to remain mostly above normal through Friday, with some areas expected to experience temperatures as much as 20 degrees Fahrenheit above normal by Friday.
Slightly cooler temperatures are expected to arrive this weekend.
According to a Reuter poll, withdrawal estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged mostly from about 25 to 35 bcf, compared with 43 bcf a year ago.
